context: Each memory is built deterministically from an integer seed. There are 180 possible action keys, named p00:a0 to p29:a5 (30 pages, each 6 actions). The exact log holds between 30 and 50 of them, called tried; the rest are untried. A Bloom filter with 128 bits and 3 hash functions is built from the tried keys: for a key, its three bit positions are sha256('<i>:<key>') mod 128 for i=0,1,2, using the first 8 bytes of the digest as a big-endian integer. The filter sets those bits for every tried key. Then, with probability 1/2, the filter is corrupted: it clears one of those three bits (chosen by the same deterministic draws) for each of 1 to 3 tried keys. A sound Bloom filter never has a false negative; a corrupted one does. The candidate keys to audit are a deterministic subset: 10 to 14 tried keys and 16 to 20 untried keys, sorted alphabetically, for 26 to 34 candidates total. The seed determines all of these via SHA-256 draws. To audit, you must, for each candidate key, know whether the Bloom filter says it was tried (all three of its positions are set) and whether the exact log says it was tried. Report as false_positives the candidates the filter says were tried but the exact log never tried; as false_negatives the candidates the exact log tried but the filter says were not tried; and corrupted as true exactly when there are any false negatives. Each key must appear at most once in each list, and no candidate may be omitted. The lists' order does not matter.
